exposure: educational intervention based on the theory of planned behavior
outcome: delivery mode choice (normal vaginal delivery vs. Cesarean section)
cohort: 87 primigravida women receiving prenatal care at obstetrics and gynecology clinics affiliated with Shiraz University of Medical Sciences.
finding: The educational intervention significantly improved participants' behavioral beliefs, outcome evaluation, attitude, control beliefs, perceived power, and perceived behavioral control scores related to delivery mode choice.
mod_finding: The study suggests that educational programs based on behavioral change theories can promote normal vaginal delivery and decrease Cesarean section rates.
